title: Egress UDP sawtooth — control plane intermittency debug journal
content:
Summary:
A recurring, rhythmic loss of control-plane reachability was observed for a single customer private-deployment cluster between 2026-03-14 and 2026-03-16. Symptoms were bursts of 20–40s control-plane RPC timeouts every ~5–7 minutes for up to 12 minutes total per hour. Downstream effect: autoscaler briefly failed health-checks and a small percentage (~2%) of host heartbeats were marked stale, causing temporary routing fallbacks to the hosted control-plane proxy.

Why this doc exists:
This is a combined incident debug journal + nascent runbook. Goal: capture exploration steps, quick mitigations used during on-call, and propose a minimal runbook to contain future sawtooth/oscillatory egress problems on on-prem/VPC installs. Not a final postmortem; intended to be iterated with customer infra and network owners.

Impact snapshot:
- Affected customer: acme-retail (private VPC, hybrid on-prem gateway)
- Duration: recurring windows 2026-03-14 22:40 UTC -> 2026-03-16 08:20 UTC (intermittent)
- User-visible: transient failures for control-plane API calls; no data loss; short-lived autoscaler misfires and delayed rollout steps
- Severity: sev-2 (customer reported production degradation)

Detection & alerts:
- Control-plane health rate decreased; alert fired on controlplane_rpc_5xx_rate > 0.5% for > 3m (Alert OPS-CTRL-RPC-03)
- On-call noticed repeating pattern on metrics dashboard: egress_bytes_udp for cluster-hosts showed periodic spikes that correlated with timeouts
- Customer SRE message at 2026-03-15 01:12 UTC reporting similar symptoms on their side

Initial hypothesis log (timeline highlights):
- 2026-03-14 22:40 UTC: First anomalous control-plane 5xx spike.
- 2026-03-15 00:10 UTC: Observed egress UDP burst from mgmt-hosts to customer gateway (dst port range ephemeral). Packet captures showed repeated ~1500B UDP packets in bursts.
- 2026-03-15 01:30 UTC: Customer firewall policy change identified as possible correlate — they applied a new flow-track rule earlier that day (customer confirmed).
- 2026-03-15 02:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: switched control-plane egress route to hosted proxy; reachability restored within 90s.
- 2026-03-15 04:20 UTC: Sawtooth resumed after ~90m; root cause not yet fixed.

Technical observations:
- Pattern: bursts of large UDP egress briefly saturating conntrack/flow tables on customer's firewall, causing ephemeral TCP control-plane handshakes to be dropped or significantly delayed when paired with NAT session limits.
- Affected protocols: control-plane uses HTTP/2 over TLS (TCP); however telemetry/heartbeat/metrics agents on hosts sent periodic UDP telemetry to a local aggregator on the customer side. Bursts aligned with batched telemetry flushes from host agents under certain load windows.
- Customer firewall device: vendor X, default conntrack table size 64k, observed conntrack exhaustion during spikes.
- No evidence of malicious traffic; traffic was legitimate telemetry but pathological in aggregate when combined with customer's egress shaping.

On-call mitigations executed (what worked):
1) Instant failover to hosted control-plane proxy route (manual policy switch) — immediate effect, lowered customer impact.
2) Coordinated temporary ACL at customer edge to prioritize TCP control-plane flows (customer applied QoS priority for control-plane IPs) — helped while we debugged.
3) Reduced telemetry batch size on one host group (rolled out agent config change) — reduced burst amplitude for those hosts.

Commands & checks used during investigation (notes for runbook):
- tcpdump/sniff: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <customer-gateway> and '(udp or tcp) and dst port 443' -w /tmp/trace.pcap
- conntrack dump on firewall (customer): sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- control-plane client check: curl -v --http2 https://controlplane.customer.internal/healthz
- metric queries: sum(rate(egress_bytes_udp[1m])) by (instance) on Grafana, correlate with controlplane_rpc_5xx_rate

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- A combination of (A) periodic large UDP telemetry flushes from our telemetry agent and (B) conservative conntrack/NAT session limits + flow-age policy on the customer's firewall led to transient conntrack exhaustion. When conntrack exhausted, new TCP connections for control-plane APIs were dropped or tokenized into long retransmit windows -> timeouts.

Permanent remediation proposals (options):
- Short term (0–7d): ship agent config change to spread telemetry flushes (randomized jitter + smaller batch size) + document config knobs for customers to rate-limit telemetry flows.
- Mid term (1–3w): add optional telemetry protocol fallback to TCP or TLS (configurable) for customers who cannot tune firewall/NAT.
- Mid–long term (1–2mo): provide an agent-side egress shaping capability that throttles UDP bursts based on configured target max conntrack entries (coordinated with customer).
- Policy docs: produce a private-deployment checklist for customers before install: recommended conntrack table size, NAT timeouts, QoS rules for control-plane TCP endpoints, and UDP telemetry guidance.

Runbook draft (for on-call):
1) Detect: if controlplane_rpc_5xx_rate > threshold and egress_bytes_udp shows spikes correlated, tag incident as 'egress-sawtooth'.
2) Contain: if possible, flip routing to hosted proxy (route-fallback) to restore control-plane availability.
3) Triage: request immediate conntrack table dump from customer and run packet capture on our hosts.
4) Short fix: ask customer to temporarily increase conntrack table size or apply QoS prioritization for TCP control-plane endpoints.
5) Mitigate from our side: roll out telemetry batch-size reduction to affected host groups; monitor for recurrence.
6) Communicate: notify customer SRE and account manager, update incident channel with timeline and mitigation steps.
7) Post-incident: open follow-up tasks (see action items).

Monitoring & alerts to create/update:
- Alert: egress_udp_burst_rate (new) — triggers when 1m-rate of egress UDP bytes per cluster > X and correlates with controlplane_rpc_5xx_rate > Y
- Dashboard: Add conntrack gauge (if customer exposes via exporter) to the private-deploy console for on-prem installs

Action items (open):
- [ ] APPLIED? push agent config canary to 10% of acme-retail hosts to validate batch-size change (owner: Tom B, due 2026-03-18)
- [ ] Create telemetry protocol fallback RFC describing TCP fallback option and deployment impact (owner: Katherine L, due 2026-04-01)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing install checklist with conntrack recommendations (owner: Miguel S, due 2026-03-22)
- [ ] Add egress_udp_burst_rate alert in observability (owner: Asha P, due 2026-03-20)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Did the customer firewall also have any ATP features that drop UDP flows aggressively under perceived flood conditions? Customer support needs to confirm firmware/ATP rules.
- Are there other customers with similar telemetry config that might trigger this? We should run a backfill scan against active private deployments.

Notes for postmortem (when finalizing):
- Capture precise conntrack counts and timestamps, include pcap excerpts.
- Enumerate tradeoffs for telemetry TCP fallback (latency/cost/complexity).
- Decide on default telemetry batching config for all on-prem installs vs making it opt-in.

Appendix (reference snippets):
- Example agent config diff to reduce batch size:
  telemetry.batch_size: 128 -> 32
  telemetry.flush_interval_ms: 10000 -> 2500
- Quick QoS rule sample for customer firewall (vendor X CLI):
  class-map match-any REDWOOD-CTRL
    match access-list 101
  policy-map PRIORITIZE-CTRL
    class REDWOOD-CTRL
      priority percent 30

If you're pairing with customer SRE during the next on-call, use this doc as the running journal; capture timestamps and small pcaps to attach. We'll convert to a formal postmortem and a short runbook entry if the mid-term mitigations look effective.

Logged-by: Asha Patel (on-call, eng-sre)

End of journal.
